 Eagle Insider AM: Remembering Dan Davis, Georgia Tech Hit Hard by Injuries, and BC WBB Takes Center Stage
 Boston College mourns legendary broadcaster Dan Davis, Georgia Tech lists 14 players out and another key defender doubtful, the Eagles' women's basketball program holds media day, and Saturday's Atlanta weather forecast looks favorable.
 AJ Black 2 
 Feels like fall doesn't it BC Nation? I enjoyed my first cider donut yesterday, nothing beats a warm one. For today's news, Boston College is mourning the loss of a familiar voice whose call of Doug Flutie's legendary Hail Mary remains one of the most memorable moments in college football history. Elsewhere, Georgia Tech is dealing with a lengthy availability report ahead of Saturday's matchup, including several players who have logged significant snaps this season. Boston College women's basketball also held its preseason media day Wednesday, while the weekend forecast in Atlanta is beginning to take shape.
 🎙️ Boston College Mourns Legendary Broadcaster Dan Davis
 Boston College football announced Wednesday that longtime broadcaster Dan Davis has passed away at the age of 84. Davis was a familiar voice to generations of Eagles fans, but his place in program history was secured on November 23, 1984, when he called Doug Flutie's unforgettable Hail Mary touchdown against Miami.
 Davis was behind the microphone as Flutie connected with Gerard Phelan on the final play, giving Boston College a stunning 47-45 victory over the Hurricanes. His radio call became part of the enduring legacy of one of college football's most celebrated plays, continuing to be replayed more than four decades later.
 Beyond that iconic moment, Davis called numerous Boston College football broadcasts and enjoyed a distinguished national broadcasting career. He was one of the original voices of ESPN Radio when the network launched in 1992, later becoming widely recognized for his SportsCenter updates.
 Known as "The Duke," Davis worked in broadcasting for nearly five decades before retiring from ESPN Radio in 2011.
 🏈 Georgia Tech Availability Report: Fourteen Players Out, Key Defensive Tackle Doubtful
 New availability report is out for the ACC, and let's look at GT. The biggest new concern is defensive tackle Tawfiq Thomas, who is listed as doubtful. The Colorado transfer has been one of Georgia Tech's most productive defenders this season, recording 37 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss and 2.5 sacks. Thomas has played 315 defensive snaps and carries an 84.6 overall PFF grade, the highest mark among Georgia Tech defenders with at least 100 snaps. His 90.9 run-defense grade is particularly impressive, while his 77.7 tackling grade and 67.8 pass-rushing grade illustrate his versatility.
 Notable Georgia Tech Players Ruled Out
 Savion Riley, Safety: Riley has played 306 defensive snaps this season, including 166 against the run and 136 in coverage. His 66.9 overall PFF grade includes a 70.2 run-defense grade and 63.3 coverage grade.   Daiquan White, Cornerback: White has logged 209 defensive snaps, including 82 in coverage. His overall PFF grade is 63.7, with a 68.6 run-defense grade and 71.5 tackling grade. Noah Carter, Defensive End: Carter has played 121 defensive snaps and owns a 76.8 overall PFF grade. His most impressive number is an 86.0 pass-rushing grade across 50 pass-rushing snaps. 
 Kyle Efford, Linebacker: Efford has played 169 defensive snaps, with 97 coming against the run. His overall PFF grade is 68.3, including a 76.2 run-defense grade. The veteran linebacker recently announced his retirement from football because of accumulated injuries.  Markell Samuel, Offensive Guard: Samuel has appeared in four games and played 164 offensive snaps, including 93 pass-blocking snaps. His overall PFF grade is 41.0, while his pass-blocking grade is just 5.9. Samuel's absence further reduces Georgia Tech's offensive line depth.  Ethan Mackenny, Offensive Tackle: Mackenny has played 73 offensive snaps across two games. His overall PFF grade is 29.9, with a 14.1 pass-blocking grade.   Malachi Hosley, Running Back: Hosley has played 29 offensive snaps across three games, earning a 72.0 overall PFF grade and a 72.9 rushing grade. 
 Other Georgia Tech Players Ruled Out
 Fenix Felton (DB), Will Kiker (DB), Kentrell Davis (WR), A.J. Hoffler (DE), Shymeik Jones (DT), Landen Marshall (DT) and Jaedyn Terry (CB).
 Questionable Players
 Jordan Walker, Defensive End: Walker has played 63 defensive snaps across two games and owns a 65.7 overall PFF grade. His 75.1 tackling grade is among his better marks.  Vincent Carroll-Jackson, Defensive Lineman: Carroll-Jackson has played 254 defensive snaps, including 142 against the run and 112 as a pass rusher. His overall PFF grade is 64.8, with a 63.8 run-defense grade.  Josh Petty, Offensive Lineman: Petty is also listed as questionable. He has not appeared in a game this season, so there are no 2026 PFF snap counts or grades to report.
 🏀 Boston College Women's Basketball Holds Preseason Media Day
 Boston College women's basketball held its preseason media day Wednesday, providing another look at the program as it prepares for its first season under head coach Kate Popovec-Goss. The Eagles enter 2026-27 with a new coaching staff and a roster undergoing significant changes. Popovec-Goss arrived in Chestnut Hill after four seasons at Bradley, where she guided the Braves to a 20-13 record in her final year.
 Boston College has added several newcomers, including international prospects and transfers, as the coaching staff works to establish its identity. Among the additions are Nuria Ausaverri, Grace Oliver, Gabriela Bernal Ortellado and Samantha Davis.
 Oliver and Popovec-Goss spoke with the media which you can see below. 
 🌤️ Atlanta Weather Forecast: Sunny and Comfortable for BC vs. Georgia Tech
 Boston College fans traveling to Atlanta for Saturday's game should find favorable football weather at Bobby Dodd Stadium. The latest forecast calls for sunny skies, temperatures in the upper 60s and relatively light winds.
 Saturday's projected high is approximately 67 degrees, with temperatures expected to drop into the upper 40s overnight. Easterly winds could reach 10 to 15 mph, but there is currently no significant rain threat in the forecast.
 Beautiful fall weather, can't beat it.
 🕰️ This Day in BC History: Eagles Knock Off Ranked Duke on Senior Night
 On October 22, 2021, No. 13 Boston College field hockey defeated No. 24 Duke 3-1 in Newton, giving the Eagles an important ACC victory on Senior Night.
 Boston College honored six players before the game, including graduate students Fusine Govaert, Elizabeth Warner and Jaime Natale, along with seniors Sky Caron, Nell Webber and Jonna Kennedy. The Eagles fell behind early when Duke scored in the opening quarter, but BC answered with less than one second remaining in the period.
 Jill Joossens scored the tying goal with just 0.6 seconds left on the clock, sending the teams into halftime tied at one. Sarah Johnson gave Boston College the lead in the third quarter, while Webber added an insurance goal in the fourth.
 The Eagles finished with a 16-13 advantage in shots, and Kennedy made four saves to secure her eighth victory of the season.
